quotes.text: "We need somebody who can actually lead here in the Central Valley. 'Data Center David' has taken over $200,000 from big tech and made it easier for them to build data centers in our backyard," Villegas said.

Artificial intelligence is changing our businesses, our schools, and our way of life, but Congress is doing little to protect workers and families against its potential dangers. We need leaders who understand its risks and are willing to fight for a future that works for everyone.
Your personal data should belong to you. Billion-dollar tech corporations should not be able to sell personal data to advertisers or use it to train their AI models without your consent.
Congress has been too slow to protect against the potential dangers of new AI technologies. Randy will fight to protect workers, families, and children from its risks.

In Congress, Randy will pass legislation mandating age verification and parental consent for high-risk AI tools, requiring bots to screen for content related to unsafe behavior, and cracking down on the creation and distribution of AI-generated child sexual abuse material with the full force of the law.

Technology should be a tool for workers, not a threat of replacement. For workers across all industries, Randy will ensure large AI companies pay their fair share in taxes and will fight to protect working people’s job security against the threat of replacement by AI.

That’s why I support a moratorium – a minimum of one year – on the construction of new data centers in the Central Valley. During that time, Congress should act to establish clear standards that put Central Valley families, workers, and resources first.

Protecting our privacy and putting guardrails on AI. The technology these facilities power cannot come at the expense of our personal information, our jobs, or our economic security. Congress needs strong rules governing how corporations collect and use our data and deploy AI.

AI can make our lives easier in some ways, but it cannot come at any cost. We have a right to control our personal information, and we have a right to control if, when, and how a new data center is built in our backyard.

“A moratorium gives the Central Valley the chance to get this right before it’s too late,” Villegas said in a written statement. “No data center should be allowed to raise families’ utility bills, threaten our water supply, exploit our personal data, or disrupt local jobs. No data center should be built without the people of the Central Valley having a real say.”
"I'm fighting for the Central Valley, Not Silicon Valley," Villegas posted. "That's Why I'm Calling For a Moratorium On Data Centers for one year at minimun."

“When everything from our healthcare to our groceries to our rent already costs too much, we can't afford to let unchecked big tech developments make life even more expensive,” Villegas said. “A moratorium gives the Central Valley the chance to get this right before it’s too late.”
“The advancement of technology ... should not be an excuse to throw our communities under the bus,”
We cannot allow AI to displace workers, and threaten life, jobs and humanity.  In Congress I'll fight to protect the Central Valley, not billionaires in Silicon Valley. https://t.co/6M8s0nI6cz

AI is advancing faster than our laws can keep up, putting our workers, environment, and children at risk. Congress must act now to regulate AI and ensure innovation never comes at the expense of our jobs, safety, or future. https://t.co/4WY2ODq0sx
